# Milestone 2 results (generated by scripts/21_m2_summary.py)

Inputs under `/data/element_runs/polyafilter_bench`. Each section names the files its numbers come from; "not run" lists the files that are absent.

Setting tags read c<COVLEN>_l<MINSNRLEN>_m<MISM>_<e or i>: COVLEN, MINSNRLEN and MISM are polyAfilter's parameters (spec 3); e is the default mode and i the -i mode (introns); l none is the remove-all control.

Missing inputs: none.

## Headline

Computed on: called cells, molecules with a member read within the cap; member cap 1,000 nt, 8/4 labels. Rule: On 1417, in each mode, the grid setting (remove-all control and off-grid published settings excluded) with the highest molecule-level sensitivity subject to specificity >= 0.95, at member cap 1000 nt and 8/4 labels; ties broken by fewer removed primary records, then by tag name. Reported on 1419 and 1179 without retuning. If no setting reaches 0.95, the frontier is reported and none is chosen.

## 1. Runs

Stage runs under memwatch (every `*.mem.json` under the base directory outside `*/original/`; a JSON written elsewhere is not found; folders kept aside from earlier runs (name containing `_pre_fix_`) are left out). This includes stage 20's createTRANS run for the remove-all control (`validation/none_control/`), an original-tool run, and its createTRANS and original-tool runs on the 1179 subset (`validation/subset_1179/`). Peak RSS is the largest sum over the process tree at a sample, so pages shared by forked workers count once per process and a peak between two samples is missed, so the peak of a shorter run reads near zero. memwatch samples every 2 s (interval_s in the files).

## 2. Truth sets

Source: `<lib>/truth/molecules_labeled.parquet` and `<lib>/truth/truth_reads.parquet` (stage 12). Labels at 8/4 A's in the 20 nt after the site; members are selected member reads (gene match, dist3_exon >= -25) by exon-aware distance; the candidates row counts them in `<lib>/members.parquet` before the cap. The truth table and the region table below cover all barcodes (every row of molecules_labeled.parquet); the tables that come from `eval/selection.json` name their population.

has_ts: a pa read of the molecule has a 10x ts tag above 0. Cell Ranger documentation, Barcoded BAM Tags (https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/analysis/outputs/cr-outputs-bam): ts is "The number of template switch oligo (TSO) nucleotides trimmed from the 5' end of read 2." Our reading: such a read reaches the 5' end of the cDNA.

## 4. Setting selection

Source: `eval/selection.json`, `eval/bootstrap.parquet`, `eval/metrics.parquet` (stage 17). Rule: On 1417, in each mode, the grid setting (remove-all control and off-grid published settings excluded) with the highest molecule-level sensitivity subject to specificity >= 0.95, at member cap 1000 nt and 8/4 labels; ties broken by fewer removed primary records, then by tag name. Reported on 1419 and 1179 without retuning. If no setting reaches 0.95, the frontier is reported and none is chosen.

Computed on: called cells, molecules with a member read within the cap.

| Mode | Chosen setting (on 1417) | Sens | Spec | Prec | Qualifying / candidates |

| default | c250_l7_m1_e | 0.093 | 0.956 | 0.986 | 146 / 189 |
| -i | c200_l10_m2_i | 0.435 | 0.951 | 0.997 | 118 / 189 |

Intergenic and antisense molecules. 'Removed at most' is the largest count over all settings in metrics.parquet (molecule level, cap 1,000, 8/4); 'never removed' is the templated count in these two regions minus that, and the ceiling is the stratum-all sensitivity if every other templated molecule were removed. Intergenic and antisense non-templated molecules count as retained negatives. Spec 3 (from the polyAfilter code, commit 5ce0098) says reads in these regions are never removed; the columns show what this data gives.

## 7. Spike-ins

Source: `<lib>/spikein/truth/molecules_labeled.parquet` (stage 14), `eval/spikein_metrics.parquet` (stage 17). spike_label comes from the distance to the annotated 3' end; label from the A count after the site. Spike label (spikein.label_spike_site) tail: within 10 nt of an annotated 3' end; internal: not tail and at least 30 nt upstream of one; other: neither, so other molecules are left out of the agreement and of the metrics (positives are internal, negatives tail). Spike-in metrics count all barcodes, whatever population the setting selection uses. 1179 has no spike-ins, so this section has no 1179 rows.

| Library | Spike label | templated | ambiguous | non-templated | total |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1417 | internal | 5,988 | 702 | 63 | 6,753 |
| 1417 | tail | 1,046 | 2,317 | 5,104 | 8,467 |
| 1417 | other | 52 | 85 | 4 | 141 |
| 1419 | internal | 6,777 | 796 | 58 | 7,631 |
| 1419 | tail | 1,249 | 2,425 | 5,292 | 8,966 |
| 1419 | other | 35 | 86 | 4 | 125 |

Agreement = (internal and templated + tail and non-templated) / internal or tail molecules labeled templated or non-templated: 1417: agreement 0.909 (11,092 of 12,201), SIRV_E0 only 0.744 (3,092 of 4,157); 1419: agreement 0.902 (12,069 of 13,376), SIRV_E0 only 0.732 (3,480 of 4,751).

- Our reading of the spike-in annotation: ERCC and long SIRV transcripts end at the contig end, so at their tail sites the 20 nt after the site are truncated and a20 cannot reach 8: their non-templated (or ambiguous) calls are forced, and they lift the pooled agreement. Only SIRV_E0 tails have full windows.
- Our reading, not tested here: a SIRV_E0 tail site can also be internal priming of a longer isoform that runs through a shorter isoform's annotated end; the annotation cannot separate the two.

Selection bias: share of labeled molecules versus share of primary records, by RE tag. RE is the region type of the alignment (E = exonic, N = intronic, I = intergenic; Cell Ranger documentation, Barcoded BAM Tags, https://www.10xgenomics.com/support/software/cell-ranger/latest/analysis/outputs/cr-outputs-bam). records_share is the share among all primary records; the duplicate-free share is the share among primary records without the PCR-duplicate flag. Both shares cover all barcodes: the records are those of every barcode, so stage 18 takes the labeled molecules of all barcodes whatever its population. The check is not repeated within called cells because stage 13 does not split the records by barcode (left for milestone 3, which builds per-cell counts):

Cell Ranger sets the duplicate flag only on reads that it counts, that is reads with a valid UMI that are confidently mapped to one gene, and among those not on the read that stands for the UMI (cellranger 9.0.1 source, lib/rust/tx_annotation/src/mark_dups.rs lines 288 to 291 and read.rs lines 560 to 568). The flag is therefore absent on every intergenic record and, in 1179 and BD67, on every intronic record and, in BD67, on every exonic record, so the shares without PCR duplicates remove duplicates only among counted reads. Milestone 3 repeats the comparison within called cells with a unit defined the same way in every region.

Spec 11 says that where labeled and unlabeled molecules differ strongly, conclusions are stated for the labeled population only; the threshold used here, a difference of more than 5 percentage points, is our choice (the milestone 1 region check uses the same value). Pairs with a difference of more than 5 percentage points: 1417 E (labeled 0.443, without duplicates 0.379, 6.3 points); 1419 E (labeled 0.439, without duplicates 0.366, 7.3 points); 1179 E (labeled 0.810, without duplicates 0.635, 17.6 points); 1179 N (labeled 0.157, without duplicates 0.289, 13.2 points); BD_nuc_211 E (labeled 0.699, without duplicates 0.594, 10.6 points); BD_nuc_211 N (labeled 0.117, without duplicates 0.191, 7.4 points); BD_nuc_213 E (labeled 0.761, without duplicates 0.620, 14.1 points); BD_nuc_213 I (labeled 0.144, without duplicates 0.201, 5.7 points); BD_nuc_213 N (labeled 0.096, without duplicates 0.179, 8.4 points); BD_nuc_215 E (labeled 0.772, without duplicates 0.634, 13.8 points); BD_nuc_215 I (labeled 0.128, without duplicates 0.183, 5.5 points); BD_nuc_215 N (labeled 0.100, without duplicates 0.183, 8.3 points).

PolyASite 3.0 proximity (share of labeled molecules by the distance in nt from the site to the nearest atlas cleavage site on the same strand; templated molecules also by A band). Proximity is reported, not used to validate the labels: the atlas is built from 10x Genomics scRNA-seq data (PolyASite 3.0, https://polyasite.unibas.ch/atlas_sc), so internally primed sites can be in it. The v3.0 documentation describes no filter on A content downstream of a site. The null row takes every molecule of the group with its site moved 1,000 nt upstream in transcript sense on the same ref and strand; its share within 10 nt is the local background at that offset, not a uniform chance level.

A content downstream of the atlas sites: our observation (`burden/polyasite_a_content.json`, stage 22, 24 of 24 atlas references): 354,361 of 18,432,135 atlas sites with a full 20 nt downstream window (1.92%) have 14 or more A's in it, against 127,400 of 18,432,135 (0.69%) for the same sites moved 1,000 nt upstream; the clusters file is not depleted of A-rich downstream sequence by this count.
